Johanan the Son of Kareah
joh-HAY-nan
proper noun
Hebrew Yohanan, “the LORD is gracious,” a captain of the remnant of Judah after the fall of Jerusalem.

📖 Biblical Definition

Johanan the son of Kareah was a captain of the forces of the remnant of Judah after the fall of Jerusalem, who began well but ended in disobedience. He warned the godly governor Gedaliah of Ishmael’s plot, and when Gedaliah was slain, Johanan pursued and rescued the captives Ishmael had taken. Then, fearing the wrath of Babylon, he and the people came to Jeremiah and asked him to enquire of the LORD their way, vowing, Whether it be good, or whether it be evil, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God (Jer 42:6). The prophet brought God’s plain answer: abide in the land and fear not; go ye not into Egypt (Jer 42:19). But Johanan and the captains would not believe it, and they took all the remnant, and Jeremiah with them, and came into the land of Egypt, for they obeyed not the voice of the LORD (Jer 43:7). The dictionary marks Johanan as the man who sought God’s counsel and then refused it, who walked down into Egypt having vowed to obey. His fall is a solemn warning against asking the will of God with a heart already set on its own way, and against fleeing to Egypt, the figure of the world’s help, by men who have not asked at God’s mouth, but strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh (Isa 30:2).

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A captain of Judah’s remnant who sought God’s counsel through Jeremiah and then disobeyed, leading the people into Egypt.

JOHANAN THE SON OF KAREAH, a captain of Judah’s remnant after the fall.

He warned Gedaliah of Ishmael’s plot and rescued the captives.

He asked Jeremiah to enquire of the LORD, vowing to obey.

God commanded them to abide in the land and not go to Egypt.

He disobeyed and led the remnant down into Egypt.

📖 Key Scripture

Jer 42:6 — "Whether it be good, or whether it be evil, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we send thee; that it may be well with us, when we obey the voice of the LORD our God."

Jer 42:19 — "The LORD hath said concerning you, O ye remnant of Judah; Go ye not into Egypt: know certainly that I have admonished you this day."

Jer 43:7 — "So they came into the land of Egypt: for they obeyed not the voice of the LORD: thus came they even to Tahpanhes."

Isa 30:2 — "That walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt!"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A figure of Scripture; the man who sought God’s counsel and refused it, a warning against asking with a heart already set.

expand to see more

Johanan has drawn no redefinition from the present age, surviving as the captain who led the remnant into Egypt against God’s word. The dictionary records him that the reader may mark the danger of seeking the will of God with a heart already resolved on its own way.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the folly of asking God’s counsel without meaning to obey it. Johanan and the people vowed to obey whatever the LORD should say, good or evil; but when the answer crossed their fears, they would not believe it, and went down into Egypt. So men still seek divine sanction for a course already chosen, and call it the will of God. The flight to Egypt is the figure of every refuge sought in the world’s strength by those who have not truly asked at God’s mouth; and Johanan’s disobedience warns that a vow of obedience is worthless where the heart is set upon its own way.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “the LORD is gracious,” Johanan names the captain who led the remnant into Egypt.

Johanan — Hebrew Yohanan, “the LORD is gracious.”

He was a captain of Judah’s remnant after the fall.

He warned Gedaliah and rescued the captives from Ishmael.

He asked Jeremiah to enquire of the LORD, vowing to obey.

He disobeyed and led the remnant into Egypt.

"Like Johanan, men still ask God’s counsel with a heart already set on their own way."

"Go ye not into Egypt: know certainly that I have admonished you this day."

"The flight to Egypt is the refuge of those who have not asked at God’s mouth."
